extracted.intended_audience: aspiring orators, rhetoricians, advocates, and students of rhetoric/classical eloquence
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for composing and performing public oratory (style, delivery, arrangement, emotional appeal) drawn from classical rhetorical discussion. Focuses on what makes an orator effective in the forum and how to judge different modes (Attic, Asiatic, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid harsh, unnatural, abject, or far-fetched expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: An orator must not use expressions that are harsh, unnatural, abject, or far-fetched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage praises speakers who entirely avoid those faults; this is presented as a baseline stylistic propriety — language should be graceful and natural rather than awkward or exaggerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of metaphor that fits its place
rubrics_metrics.description: Abound in metaphor, but only such metaphors 'as did not appear to usurp a post that belonged to another, but only to occupy their own.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphors should enliven without intruding on or replacing other necessary elements of expression; they should be appropriate to the subject and not forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delicacy of style without looseness or tedium ('numerous' style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Delicacies are displayed not in a loose and disfluent style but in one 'strictly numerous, without either appearing to be so, or running on with a dull uniformity of sound.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style should show variety and ornamentation while avoiding both puffed diffuseness and monotonous repetition; the reader/listener should not perceive labor or uniform tedium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of figures and ornaments ('figures')
rubrics_metrics.description: Be master of the various ornaments of language and sentiment (the Greek 'figures'), thereby enlivening and embellishing style as forensic decorations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skillful use of rhetorical figures (devices of speech) adds ornamentation appropriate to judicial/forensic context; misuse or overuse would be implied anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discernment of the real point of debate
rubrics_metrics.description: Readily discover, upon all occasions, what was the real point of debate and where the stress of the argument lay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective orators focus on the decisive issues; arranging emphasis to highlight the pivotal points is a mark of artful judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artful arrangement of ideas and genteel action
rubrics_metrics.description: Method of ranging ideas extremely artful; action genteel; manner engaging and sensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrangement (structure) and delivery (gesture, comportment) should be polished and suit the audience; 'genteel' action signals controlled, appropriate physicality rather than clowning or excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threefold purpose of oratory: instruct, please, and move the passions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the business of an Orator to instruct, to please, and to move the passions; the speaker should aim at all three.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction and pleasing are necessary but subordinate to the capacity to move passions; a complete orator combines clarity, charm, and emotional persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of moving the passions (pathos)
rubrics_metrics.description: The moving and alarming of the passions is of much greater efficacy than instructing or pleasing; destitution of this is a serious defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a prosecutor who narrates a plot calmly fails to convince because he does not arouse expected emotional signs; successful pleading often hinges on the ability to inflame or restrain emotions as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visible emotion and gesture to authenticate feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Expression of resentment, ardour, eagerness, disorder of mind, emotion in looks and gesture (smiting thigh/forehead, stamping foot) are natural signs that engage the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of physical signs when emotion is expected undermines credibility; appropriate, authentic gestures and visible emotion strengthen persuasive effect; overacting would be implied as counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turning a personal defect into a rhetorical advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use natural defect (e.g., calmness) as an argument to invalidate opponent's charge when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives the tactical example of using the prosecutor's calmness as evidence of fabrication — shows how contextual interpretation of demeanor can be used strategically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-refinement that evaporates force
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not be so minute and nice a critic upon yourself that, while labouring to correct and refine language, you suffer all the force and spirit of it to evaporate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive self-editing and polish can strip speech of vigor and emotional power; balance refinement with preservation of natural force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness and propriety as one acceptable Attic trait
rubrics_metrics.description: An accurate, judicious, neat, and compact but unembellished style may be considered 'Attic' and has a legitimate place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage defends a restrained Atticism (correctness/propriety) as valid, while warning that Atticism is broader than mere neatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atticism is plural and model-dependent
rubrics_metrics.description: Attic Speakers are not all of the same cast (Demosthenes, Lysias, Hyperides, Aeschines differ); imitation must be specific because their characters are opposite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing an Attic model, decide which exemplar you mean to imitate; attempting to imitate conflicting models at once is incoherent and doomed to fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose models appropriate to genre (history vs judicial pleading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thucydides is an exact and stately historian but not a model for conducting a judicial process; choose models suited to your purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different genres demand different tones: historians and pleaders employ different registers; misapplied imitation yields poor results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid a dry, niggardly 'Atticism' that fails in public forums
rubrics_metrics.description: A half-starved, dry, and niggardly turn of expression, though neat, will fail to attract popular attention in the open Forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public pleading requires fullness and elevation; a merely neat style may satisfy connoisseurs but not a crowd or high-stakes tribunal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public success measured by audience response
rubrics_metrics.description: The Orator who fills the benches, hushes the audience into profound silence, excites plaudits, bursts of laughter, or transports of passion is truly Attic and successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience reaction (attendance, silence, applause, laughter, visible emotion) is an external metric of an orator's effectiveness in public settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony: appropriate in some contexts, reprehensible in others
rubrics_metrics.description: Continued irony (à la Socrates) can be humorous and becoming in dialogues but may be reprehensible when used in a professed History or in judicial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use irony with caution; genre and audience determine whether it aids or undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory and verbal recall
rubrics_metrics.description: An excellent memory: able to repeat privately composed material without notes and remember opponents' words without prompter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong memory enables precise repetition and rebuttal; it is a prized professional faculty in an orator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passionate dedication and daily practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Inflamed with passionate fondness for the profession; would not suffer a day to elapse without speaking in the Forum or composing something at home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistent, daily exercise (speaking, composing, declamation) is fundamental to developing oratorical skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearness and accuracy in stating and summarizing points
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncommon clearness and accuracy in stating the points to speak to; a neat and easy manner of collecting the substance of what had been said by opponents and by himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity and precise distillation of arguments (both one's own and opponents') are practical hallmarks of an accomplished pleader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of words, flow of periods, and copious elocution
rubrics_metrics.description: Elegant choice of words, agreeable flow in periods, and a copious elocution, partly natural and partly acquired by rhetorical exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lexical choice and sentence rhythm (periods) contribute to persuasiveness and elegance; cultivate vocabulary and syntactic fluency through disciplined practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive mastery of the subject and careful division
rubrics_metrics.description: A most retentive view of the subject; always divided and parcelled it out with the greatest exactness; seldom overlooked anything proper to support or refute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough command of material and systematic organization (division of points) prevent missing crucial arguments and facilitate thorough rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice quality and measured gesture
rubrics_metrics.description: Sweet and sonorous voice; gesture had rather more art in it, and was more exactly managed, than is requisite to an Orator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vocal timbre and controlled, artful gesture enhance delivery; gestures should be well-managed rather than exaggerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temper and bodily management: moderate vehemence
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderate the vehemence of voice and action; correct excessive ardour to avoid physical danger and improve ease of speaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel/study and training (e.g., in Asia, Rhodes) are recommended to refine voice and action; manage physicality for stamina and clarity rather than uncontrolled exertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrain luxuriant imagination within due channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrain the luxuriancy of a juvenile imagination, always ready to overflow its banks, within due and proper channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative exuberance must be disciplined so ornamentation aids rather than overwhelms the argument; teachers (Molo, Demetrius) can correct excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from varied masters and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaim in Greek more often than Latin because Greek furnishes a greater variety of ornaments; study under different masters to import useful elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure to diverse rhetorical traditions and languages broadens stylistic resources; imitation should be selective and adapted to one’s own idiom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt style to forum, audience, and occasion
rubrics_metrics.description: A crowded Forum requires a lively, animated orator able to exert voice to the highest pitch; different settings demand different tones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibrate tone, ornament, and action to the venue (open Forum vs private assembly vs history-writing); popular settings demand more animation, closed/learned contexts may favor restraint.
